description:
As a security auditor, I need to perform a basic check on the permissions of users in an SQLite database using the command line interface. There's an SQLite database file at /home/user/security_audit/permissions.db. 1. Connect to the /home/user/security_audit/permissions.db database using the SQLite CLI. 2. The database contains a table named user_permissions with three columns: username (TEXT), role (TEXT), and can_edit (INTEGER, where 1 means permission granted and 0 means denied). 3. Run a query to list all users with can_edit permission set to 1. Output requirement: Write the results to a new file named /home/user/security_audit/can_edit_users.log, including both the column names and the data, in the following precise format (columns separated by the pipe character " | ", no extra whitespace, one user per line): 
username | role | can_edit
[username1] | [role1] | [can_edit1]
[username2] | [role2] | [can_edit2]
...
Replace [usernameX], [roleX], [can_editX] with the actual values from the table for each matching user. Make sure that the /home/user/security_audit/can_edit_users.log file is created with the correct contents as specified above.
truth:
Before the task starts, the following file and directory must exist:
- Directory: /home/user/security_audit
- File: /home/user/security_audit/permissions.db

The /home/user/security_audit/permissions.db SQLite database contains:
- A table named "user_permissions" with columns:
    - username (TEXT)
    - role (TEXT)
    - can_edit (INTEGER)

The table "user_permissions" contains exactly:
username   | role     | can_edit
-----------|----------|---------
alice      | admin    | 1
bob        | staff    | 0
carol      | editor   | 1
dave       | guest    | 0

After the agent completes the task, the file /home/user/security_audit/can_edit_users.log must contain exactly (no trailing whitespace or blank lines):

username | role | can_edit
alice | admin | 1
carol | editor | 1

Permissions:
- The /home/user/security_audit directory and all its contents are owned by user "user" and are writable by them.
